newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan refinery shuts one unit for blast inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan refinery shuts one unit for blast inquiry.

text.p: State-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp shut down one of two production units at its northern Taiwan refinery on Monday to allow an official investigation of a gas explosion that killed one worker, executives said.
It was not known how long the shutdown would last, a CPC executive told Reuters by telephone from the refinery at Taoyuan.
"The blast did not cause much damage to the facility, but we still shut down the plant because of the death," company spokeswomen Ho Li-chiung said by telephone.
Police and labour officials were at the refinery to conduct the investigation, which could take a few days.

The refinery's principal product is jet fuel for the Taiwan's main international airport nearby but Ho said the company's jet fuel supplies would not run short as the plant's second unit was still running.
Chinese Petroleum also produces jet fuel at its refinery in southern Kaohsiung.
A Chinsese Petroleum worker was killed on Monday in a gas explosion that blasted away the door of a pump control room. The door struck and fatally injured the worker.
The Taoyuan refinery turns out 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel a month at full capacity.
